newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cultus jumps on Otway oil, say analysts.
newsitem.headline: Cultus jumps on Otway oil, say analysts.

text.p: Shares in Cultus Petroleum NL rose 19 cents, or almost 10 percent, on Friday as the oil and gas junior pushed back above the A$2 mark.
Cultus shares were trading at A$2.12 at 1.00 p.m. (0200 GMT).
Analysts said the rise followed the discovery of a small amount of oil in the Skull Creek West No. 1 well in Victoria's Otway Basin, which had boosted hopes of a commercial discovery.
"It's the first time they have recovered oil in that permit ... and they have a dominant position in the basin," one analyst said.

However, the find was unlikely to lead to a commercial oilfield, he added. "It just increases people's confidence that they have still got a chance of finding an oilfield down there rather than all the gas they have been finding."
In a release to the stock exchange on Thursday, Cultus said a wireline sample recovered 4.5 litres of gas, 0.4 litres of oil and 9.0 litres of water from the Eumerella formation.
Cultus shares were boosted last month by its participation in Permit WA-241-P in the Browse Basin offshore Western Australia, which reported an oil discovery from its Cornea well.
